targets.name: Mill Creek 5

targets.name: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind commercial project
targets.targetEvidence: The operator timeline identifies 2026–2027 project construction and commissioning. First power in March 2026 does not mean full completion; the retained target is 2027, without asserting an exact day.

cost.name: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind commercial project
cost.capacityBasis: Operator-reported electric generating capacity; not annual energy production
cost.costBasis: Estimated total project cost excluding financing; includes $0.1 billion contingency
cost.facts: Dominion’s June 30, 2026 quarterly filing gives approximately $11.7 billion estimated total project cost, excluding financing and including $0.1 billion contingency. It supersedes earlier $10.7 billion/$11.5 billion estimates. The commercial project rating is approximately 2,600 MW, separate from the older 12 MW pilot; first power occurred March 23, 2026 while construction continues.
extra: Operator records first power March 23, 2026; full-project completion is expected in 2027.
The operator identifies approximately 2.6 GW for the commercial project.
cost.costFacts: Published project-specific cost for Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind commercial project: USD 1.17e+10. Basis: Estimated total project cost excluding financing; includes $0.1 billion contingency.
cost.capacityFacts: Published electric generating project rating for Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind commercial project: 2600 MW. Basis: Operator-reported electric generating capacity; not annual energy production.

targets.name: Empire Wind 1
targets.targetEvidence: Equinor identifies an expected commercial-operation date in 2027 for Empire Wind 1.

cost.name: Empire Wind 1
cost.capacityBasis: Operator-reported electric generating capacity; not annual energy production
cost.costBasis: Total capital investment including terminal-use fees and expected tax credits; tax-credit-adjusted, not gross pre-credit cost
cost.facts: Equinor describes total Empire Wind capital expenditure estimated at $5 billion after tax credits, covering 54 bottom-fixed turbines and the Brooklyn cable landfall. This is a tax-credit-adjusted estimate, not gross pre-credit cost and not the over-$3 billion financing package. Empire Wind 1 has an 810 MW generation rating and documented offshore construction; full operation is targeted for 2027.
extra: Official project announcement identifies 810 MW and distinguishes financing from project capital expenditure.
cost.costFacts: Equinor January 2, 2025 publishes approximately USD5 billion expected total capital investment, including South Brooklyn Marine Terminal use fees and the effect of expected future investment tax credits. The financing package above USD3 billion is separate.
cost.capacityFacts: Published electric generating project rating for Empire Wind 1: 810 MW. Basis: Operator-reported electric generating capacity; not annual energy production.

targets.name: Kingston combined-cycle replacement plant
targets.targetEvidence: TVA’s FY2025 filing identifies physical construction of the 1,500 MW Kingston combined-cycle replacement plant and expected operation by the end of calendar 2027.

cost.name: Kingston combined-cycle replacement plant
cost.capacityBasis: Operator-reported electric generating capacity; not annual energy production
cost.costBasis: Sum of disclosed spent and forecast remaining project expenditure; approximately $2.9 billion
cost.facts: TVA FY2025 Form 10-K publishes $1.8 billion spent and $1.1 billion expected additional spending on the 1,500 MW Kingston combined-cycle plant as of September 30, 2025. Their sum is approximately $2.9 billion. This total is arithmetic on disclosed project amounts, not a benchmark estimate. Battery RFPs, proposed expansions and the wider campus rating are not included.

Battery RFPs, proposed expansions and the wider campus rating are not included.
cost.capacityFacts: Kingston combined-cycle replacement plant: published generating capacity 1500 MW. Operator-reported electric generating capacity; not annual energy production
cost.physicalFacts: TVA explicitly states it is constructing the 1,500 MW combined-cycle plant, targeting the end of 2027. The capacity is for the combined-cycle plant, not all units at the Kingston site.

cost.capacityBasis: Operator-reported electric generating capacity; not annual energy production
cost.costBasis: Unit 1 plus shared infrastructure; includes interest, escalation and contingency

targets.name: Hinkley Point C
targets.targetEvidence: EDF’s February 20, 2026 presentation organises Hinkley Unit 1 for operation in 2030 and Unit 2 twelve months later. The 3.3 GW capacity and GBP35 billion estimate in 2015 sterling cover both reactors; neither is represented as wholly delivered by 2030.

cost.name: Hinkley Point C
cost.capacityBasis: EDF presentation rounded electric project rating: 3.3 GW
cost.costBasis: Completion estimate in constant 2015 GBP; not nominal 2026 GBP
cost.facts: EDF’s February 20, 2026 results presentation labels Hinkley Point C as a 3.3 GW EPR project and estimates completion cost at £35 billion in 2015 sterling. A 12-month delay could add around £1 billion in the same price basis. Both reactors have documented construction progress; Unit 1 is organized for 2030, with Unit 2 twelve months later. This is actual construction, not an announcement-only proposal.
cost.costFacts: Published project-specific cost for Hinkley Point C: GBP 3.5e+10. Basis: Completion estimate in constant 2015 GBP; not nominal 2026 GBP.
cost.capacityFacts: Published electric generating project rating for Hinkley Point C: 3300 MW. Basis: EDF presentation rounded electric project rating: 3.3 GW.
